newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ABC in A$30 mln Optus satellite deal.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ABC in A$30 mln Optus satellite deal.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Wednesday Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) has chosen Optus' Aurora digital satellite system to deliver remote area television services in a deal worth about A$30 million.

Optus said the five-year deal with the government owned broadcaster will result in the ABC delivering TV and radio services such as Radio National and ABC FM via Aurora using both Direct to Home (DTH) and terrestrial re-transmission methods.
Optus is 25 percent owned by Mayne Nickless Ltd, 24.5 percent each owned by Cable and Wireless Plc and BellSouth Corp. The rest is owned by local investors.
The telecommunications group said it has also signed a satellite deal with Telecasters Australia Ltd (TAL) where TAL will use Aurora to broadcast in remote areas of Queensland and New South Wales.
